channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Presents Proposals to Improve Administrative Justice System
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed proposals for further improving Uzbekistan's administrative justice system. Since July 2017, administrative courts have handled nearly 150,000 cases, overturning over 70,000 illegal state body decisions and issuing 27,000 private rulings.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase Electricity Production Capacity to 46.1 GW by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to reach 46.1 GW of electricity production capacity by 2030, generating nearly 129 billion kWh annually. Capacity is projected to rise to 57.2 GW by 2035. This expansion is driven by economic growth, population increase, and rising energy consumption.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Health Ministry Plans Pilot Health Check-ups for Civil Servants
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Health plans to launch pilot health check-ups for state and municipal employees starting October 1. Deputy Minister Nurbek Bukuev stated that nationwide implementation is challenging, but they aim to expand the program based on pilot results.

item.title: Tashkent region to increase drinking water and sewage tariffs starting October 3
item.description: The Tashkent regional council approved new tariffs for drinking water and sewage services. For most residents, the price per cubic meter of water will increase by 19% to 3100 Uzbek soums, and sewage services by 15% to 1500 Uzbek soums. The new rates take effect on October 3.

item.title: Program for safe and respectful work environment implemented in labor sphere
item.description: A presidential decree introduces a program to ensure a safe and respectful work environment across all forms of ownership. An information portal will launch by December 1 for online reporting of pressure and violence in the workplace.

item.title: Tajikistan's Migration Ministry Warns Against Sending Money to Unknown Individuals
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Labor and Migration representative office in Russia urges Tajik migrants not to transfer money to unknown accounts or contact suspicious groups. The office warns of artificial intelligence-generated content used by fraudulent funds and banned organizations to solicit money and recruit migrants for illegal activities. Russian law carries severe penalties for such actions.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Attends UN General Assembly Debate Opening
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov participated in the opening of the general debate at the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York on September 22nd. The presidential press service reported his attendance.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Presidents Discussed Relations and Regional Issues
item.description: The Presidents of Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan held a phone call on September 22. They discussed strengthening bilateral relations, expanding trade and economic cooperation, and regional issues. The leaders also exchanged views on upcoming summits, including the Central Asia and Azerbaijan consultative meeting and the CIS summit in Turkmenistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Era for Entrepreneurship with Focus on Prevention and Opportunities
item.description: Uzbekistan is shifting towards a new era for entrepreneurship, moving from control to prevention and from barriers to opportunities. A presidential decree introduced a three-year moratorium on inspections for small businesses, strengthening legal guarantees and financial support to foster business activity.

item.title: Uzbekistan Emphasizes Soil Analysis for Food Security and Soil Fertility
item.description: Uzbekistan's Center for Agrochemistry and Soil Analysis is conducting systematic studies to ensure food security and soil fertility. In 2021-2026, 3.3 million hectares of arable land were analyzed, with electronic agrochemical maps created for 2.8 million hectares. Over 1,800 tons of substandard fertilizers were prevented from reaching fields.

item.title: Hungarian Prime Minister Opposes Oil Storage Facility Construction for Ukraine
item.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán has declared his opposition to the construction of an oil storage facility within Hungary intended for Ukraine. Orbán stated that his party, 'Tisza', will not permit such construction while it is in power, emphasizing his firm stance against the project.

item.title: Uzbekistan to launch portal for workplace pressure and discrimination complaints
item.description: Uzbekistan will gradually implement the 'Safe and Respectful Working Environment' program, designed to protect employees from pressure, violence, discrimination, and harassment in the workplace.

item.title: Bishkek auto repair worker detained on suspicion of drug trafficking
item.description: A resident of the Chuy region was detained in Bishkek on suspicion of involvement in the illegal trafficking of narcotic drugs.

item.title: Illegal tobacco sales worth 2.8 billion Uzbek soms seized in Namangan
item.description: Authorities in Namangan have stopped the sale of illegal tobacco products valued at 2.8 billion Uzbek soms.

item.title: Tajikistan and Germany Discuss Expanding Labor Migration Opportunities
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Labor, Migration, and Employment met with a German company representative to discuss expanding cooperation in labor migration. They focused on creating transparent selection mechanisms for the German labor market, including candidate training and language preparation. Both sides expressed readiness to continue dialogue and strengthen ties.

item.title: 700 delegates to be elected for Kyrgyzstan's fifth People's Kurultai
item.description: Preparations are underway in Kyrgyzstan for the fifth People's Kurultai. A total of 700 delegates will be elected based on established quotas to attend the event.

item.title: China Hosts Meeting on Uzbekistan's Sustainable Aviation Fuel Production Project
item.description: In Ningbo, China, Allied Biofuels held a FEED meeting for its sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and e-SAF production project in Uzbekistan, valued at $6.1 billion. Representatives from Sinopec, Topsoe, Sasol, and Plug Power attended. Sinopec Engineering Group will conduct FEED, with Topsoe and Sasol providing key technologies, and Plug Power supplying electrolyzer systems.

item.title: Warehouse manager at Namangan kindergarten accused of raping a 5-year-old girl
item.description: A warehouse manager at a state kindergarten in Uzbekistan's Namangan region is accused of raping a 5-year-old girl. A criminal case was initiated on September 12 under Article 118, Part 4 of the Criminal Code. The suspect has been detained and a pre-trial detention measure imposed.

item.title: Uzbek team presents atomic city concept at Global HackAtom championship
item.description: A team from Uzbekistan, "Synthesis," presented a concept for an atomic city at the Global HackAtom international student championship in Yekaterinburg. Their model city utilizes a nuclear power plant for electricity, heat, desalination, nuclear medicine, and industrial production, aiming for self-sufficiency.

item.title: Uzbekistan to expand citizens' right to appeal against state bodies in administrative court
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering expanding citizens' ability to appeal against state bodies in administrative courts. Proposals include introducing four types of claims and allowing appeals without time limits in certain cases, according to a meeting chaired by the President.

item.title: Uzbekistan may grant citizens the right to appeal local government regulations in court
item.description: Uzbekistan may grant citizens the right to directly appeal normative legal acts of local authorities in administrative courts. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed proposals to enhance administrative justice, which aims to strengthen judicial oversight and protect citizens' rights.

item.title: Diesel Fuel Imports from Russia to Tajikistan Increased 3.5 Times
item.description: Imports of diesel fuel from Russia to Tajikistan have increased by 3.5 times. This significant rise in imports is reported to have addressed the shortage of diesel fuel, often referred to as 'salyarka', within the country.

item.title: Two new deputy defense ministers appointed in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan has appointed two new deputy defense ministers. Colonel Qahramonjon Zoidov has been appointed deputy minister for armament and weaponization, previously heading the Institute of Land Forces at the Defense and Armament University. Colonel of Justice Jaxongir Muratov has been appointed deputy minister for compliance and internal anti-corruption control, having previously served as first deputy military prosecutor.

item.title: Tajik President congratulates Putin on Russian Duma elections
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon congratulated Russian President Vladimir Putin on the successful completion of the State Duma elections. The Tajik president called the elections an important event, noting public support for Putin's course towards sustainable socio-economic development. Rahmon expressed Tajikistan's commitment to further developing Tajik-Russian relations and cooperation.

item.title: Tajikistan and China discuss transport cooperation and SCO logistics
item.description: Tajikistan's Chamber of Commerce and Industry met with China's Embassy in Tajikistan to discuss trade and investment. They focused on the upcoming SCO Transport and Logistics exhibition in Dushanbe, inviting Chinese companies to participate.

item.title: Kyrgyz Stock Exchange to launch Islamic securities trading platform
item.description: The Kyrgyz Stock Exchange and the Association of Islamic Finance signed an agreement to develop a platform for Islamic financial instruments. This initiative aims to issue sukuk and position Kyrgyzstan as a regional Islamic economy center, attracting international investment.

item.title: Kamchybek Tashiev loses influence in Kyrgyz football; business shares transferred
item.description: Kamchybek Tashiev, a major football patron in Kyrgyzstan, has reportedly exited the Football Federation after stepping down as head of the GKNB. Journalists found that Tashiev's associates have transferred shares in football academies and a residential complex to individuals linked to the president.

item.title: Gas pipeline to China via Tajikistan discussed again in Dushanbe
item.description: A project for a gas pipeline to China via Tajikistan was again discussed in Dushanbe. The article aims to explain the nature of this project and its significance for Tajikistan.

item.title: MP urges reduction in pension payments via post due to high costs
item.description: A member of parliament is urging the reduction of pension payments through the postal service, citing high associated costs. In 2025, nearly 430 million som were spent on postal pension payouts, compared to 248 million via banks.

item.title: CIS Strategic Group Discusses Monitoring of International Transport Corridors
item.description: The second meeting of the CIS Council on Railway Transport's Strategic Group for the Development of International Transport Corridors was held in Moscow. Representatives from several member states, including Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, participated. Discussions focused on monitoring corridor operations and automating processes.

item.title: Prosecutor General's Office Uncovers Violations in Social Order Implementation
item.description: The Prosecutor General's Office of the Kyrgyz Republic has identified systemic violations in the implementation of the state social order during an anti-corruption law compliance check. The value of the social order was 3.7 million soms.

item.title: Kapitalbank Opens US Dollar Correspondent Account with BNY Mellon
item.description: Kapitalbank has opened a US dollar correspondent account with The Bank of New York Mellon (BNY), one of the world's largest financial institutions and oldest US banks. This move facilitates international transactions for the bank.

item.title: Latvia Blocks Removal of EU Sanctions on Alisher Usmanov, Proposes Extending Russia Sanctions
item.description: Latvia has blocked the lifting of EU sanctions against Alisher Usmanov. A proposal was made to simultaneously extend sanctions against Russia for three years in exchange for lifting sanctions on Usmanov and Fridman. France and Slovakia had requested the lifting of sanctions on the Russian billionaires.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Congratulates Turkmenistan President on Birthday, Discusses Bilateral Relations
item.description: Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated the President of Turkmenistan on his birthday via a phone call. During the conversation, they discussed pressing issues concerning the further development of Uzbek-Turkmen friendship, good neighborliness, and strategic partnership relations.

item.title: Citizen Who Fought in Ukraine Sentenced to Over Four Years in Uzbekistan
item.description: A 37-year-old Uzbek citizen, who fought for Russia in the Ukraine conflict, has been sentenced to four years and four months in prison. He signed a contract with the Russian Ministry of Defense while serving time in Russia, subsequently fighting in Ukraine. He sustained injuries from a mine explosion during combat.

item.title: Trump Canceled Strike on Houthis; Yemen Rebels Vow to Target Only 'Enemy Saudi' Ships
item.description: Former US President Trump reportedly canceled a planned strike against Yemen's Houthis at the last minute. In response, the Houthis stated they would only target ships from 'enemy Saudi Arabia' in the Red Sea, while warning of their international combat capabilities. The specifics of the cancellation were not detailed.

item.title: Tajikistan launches pest control center for agricultural crops
item.description: Tajikistan's Academy of Sciences has inaugurated a new center for integrated pest management of agricultural crops. The facility is equipped with modern technology and aims to enhance biological and food security. Its establishment aligns with national priorities for scientific research and agricultural development.

item.title: Prize Ram Sold for One Million Dollars in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A pedigree ram of the "Arashan" meat-fattening breed was sold for one million dollars in Kyrgyzstan at an international festival. The ram, acquired in Kazakhstan for $150,000 in 2023, is a descendant of a famous sire. The "Arashan" breed was officially registered in Kyrgyzstan in 2021.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans AI-Driven Urban Greening Initiative
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to implement the '3-30-300' principle for urban greening, aiming for increased tree visibility and canopy cover. An AI module, Yashil AI, will analyze soil, climate, and water data to optimize planting and identify risks. The initiative will initially be piloted in Tashkent, Bukhara, and Samarkand regions.

item.title: Prominent Tajik Journalist and Politician Otakhon Latifi Murdered in Dushanbe
item.description: Otakhon Latifi, a well-known Tajik journalist, politician, and member of the National Reconciliation Commission, was killed in Dushanbe at age 62. He began his career in journalism, worked for prominent Soviet publications, and later served as Deputy Chairman of the Council of Ministers of Tajikistan, playing a role in stabilizing the country. Latifi was a key participant in peace talks and continued his peace efforts after leaving Tajikistan during the civil war.
